To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. we propose a new approach to monocular 2D-to-3D pose estimation, 2. it outperforms state of the art approaches in terms of structure and prediction accuracy and 3. it is the first approach that learns a structured representation for 3D pose.

(i) we introduce the first Deep Learning architecture for structured prediction in monocular 3-D human pose estimation and (ii) we show that our approach outperform state-of-the-art methods both in terms of 3D structure preservation and prediction performance.

(1) a Deep Learning regression approach for 3D pose prediction can be trained in an end-to-end fashion, without the need of a structured learning framework, and (2) a latent pose representation that accounts for joint dependencies can be learned in an unsupervised way, by training an autoencoder on a large amount of unlabeled data.
